data.name: Rati
data.gender_notes: Rati is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A goddess of love and desire, personification of love and wife of Lord Kamadeva. She is the embodiment of the romantic longing and sexual desire that every human being feels. The name Rati carries the meaning “Night” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Rati usually hope their child will grow to embody night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine energy, represents the passionate and loving side of women.
data.etymology: Rati belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rati total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Rati, in Hindu mythology, is considered as the Goddess of Love and desire. She is described as the embodiment of emotion, passion, and sexuality. Her symbolic representation can be found in various art forms, from temples to dance and poetry. Her story is intricately linked to the Hindu concept of love, which is considered to be an essential aspect of human life.
data.spiritual_significance: spiritually, Rati represents the deep emotional and physical connections that exist between beings. She embodies the desire for love, union, and companionship that is a fundamental part of the human experience. Her presence serves as a reminder of the importance of balancing both physical and emotional desires, and the need for spiritual growth and self-realization to foster deeper connections with others. Furthermore, her union with Lord Kamadeva, the god of love, symbolizes the transformative power of love in shaping individuals and relationships.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rati is the personification of marital love and desire in Hindu mythology. She is the wife of Amourous God Cupid or Kama, and they are believed to have ignited the first spark of desire in the hearts of the gods and humans. Rati is also known as the queen of night, representing the sensuality and mystery of the dark. She is the embodiment of passionate love and sensuality, inspiring union and harmony.
